answer: Coordination-depth pricing. Each identity's price to act is a function of how many other identities must co-sign within a fixed window before its action executes: agents gather on a shared knoll of pending intents, and the system charges the full depth of the co-signature canyon between intent and execution. Isolated sybils wander without counterparties, so reaching depth means paying every co-signer's fee plus latency; cost scales with the square of coordinated identities, not one bond.
